_note: Persisted round-trip proof (run live on a real plant, Aug 2026, scratch panel deleted afterwards). Flow: load source panel -> IWDIE export (collect + embed bg) -> create scratch panel client-side -> IWDIE Insert JSON -> host 'Compile Panel for Plant' (iw_save -> save_xml.htm popup -> POST iw_save_ctrls.php) -> server fetch-back -> full page reload -> host load of the scratch panel -> delete via iw_remove_panel.php.

stored_doc_fetchback.fingerprint_vs_source_export: IDENTICAL across [obj_id, driver_id, posLeft, posTop, posWidth, posHeight, zIndex, unit_id, alias_text, tag_text, link_tag, sub_group] for all 54 objects (object_N names renumber by design)

cross_plant_insert._flow: Export the 54-object panel on the source plant -> Insert JSON on a scratch canvas on a DIFFERENT plant (canvas-only, no save).
cross_plant_insert.rebind_prompt: Fired exactly as designed: 'This panel comes from plant <src> - you are on plant <dst>. Rewrite 54 driver ids from <src>_... to <dst>_...?'
notes: Rebound ids keep the full address path (<dst>_AK3_AKC_0_11_1_0_7) - whether that address exists on the target plant is resolved by the designer at link/compile time, as documented (checkDriver does not validate).

org_image_name keeps the source-plant-prefixed FILENAME (e.g. 10113_oversikt_v3.png) - cosmetic only, since the image data itself is embedded and applied; a later compile posts that name as 'Original Image Name' metadata.

findings: iw_save_ctrls.php IGNORED the posted visible=0 - the new panel row came back visible=1. Panel visibility for new compiles is not controllable from the save popup; change it afterwards (picture manager / Change Panel Order flow) if the panel must stay hidden.
The compiled store keeps the JSON doc + the base64 image exactly as posted - iw_load_ctrls.php?format=json is a faithful read-back of upload_json.

Playwright note: #submit1 fails Playwright's stability check (animated preview image) - drive the popup with evaluate(() => saveXML()) after setting #visible; wait for submit1.disabled === false first (it enables ~500ms after the review table builds).
